expected.how_to_read: One row per sheet value that Vesper's export of 2026-09-22 does not print as the sheet writes it, per SKU column, derived on 2026-09-24 from the PDF's text layer and from references/workbook/spec/experience-2-cc.json. `sheet` is the value the spec reads (the SKU's column, else Common specs); `pdf` is what the page prints where that value belongs, with a long dash read as empty. A row is matched on tab, column, component, field and cause; `sheet`, `pdf` and `note` are for the reader. spec_diff.py with --expected exits 0 only when it reports exactly these rows and the two page assertions below. A row on either side of that is a finding about the script or about this file, settled by looking at the PDF, never by editing the sheet.

reading.header: CMF NUMBER, COLLECTION, PRODUCT NAME, PRODUCT CODE, EAN CODE, EDIT DATE, DRAWN and the two CHECKED cells are read as the banner rows CMF number, Collection, Product Name, Product Code, EAN code, Edit Date, Drawn by, Checked by 1 and Checked by 2, in that order
reading.blocks: each component heading is read as the component header it stands for; inside a block Vesper prints four labels, read as the sheet's Material, Finish or Finishing, Colour and Artwork fields. A sheet field with none of those names has no place of its own on Vesper's page. Material and Finishing match on every page and have no row
reading.pages_note: Columns D and F are both titled 'Ice blu marble'; the two pages are told apart only by their order and by the artwork colour (Silver on D, White on F)

causes.placeholder in the sheet: the sheet's yellow cell is still a placeholder and the PDF prints it empty; named here, not in spec-fields.md's table
causes.notes under Artwork: spec-fields.md; fields outside Vesper's alias map land in notes, and notes are printed under the Artwork label
causes.truncated code: spec-fields.md; the cell cut down to its code, whether codes after the first or words before it were lost
